zh.sourceText: 某媒体调查显示，78% 的受访者支持在市中心修建新的高架桥。报道称，市民普遍支持这一工程，因此项目应当尽快动工。这项调查由市交通局出资开展。【gap:gap1】

textRefs.reason_1: 78% 的受访者支持在市中心修建新的高架桥
textRefs.gap1_correct: 受访者均通过交通局官网主动报名，样本严重偏向支持者
textRefs.distractor_1: 这项调查由市交通局出资开展

gap1: 受访者均通过交通局官网主动报名，样本严重偏向支持者
高架桥的建设工期预计为三年
市政府此前多次召开公开听证会

hints: 报道里有什么没说？关键信息被撕掉了
想一想：「78%」这个数字可信吗？调查对象是怎么选出来的？
谁出资、受访者从哪来——这些通常会被有意无意地省略
zh.explanation: 报道省略了最关键的信息：受访者是通过交通局官网主动报名的，样本严重偏向本来就支持工程的人。没有这条信息，「78% 支持」很可能只是「本来支持的人」的声音，而不是全体市民的意见。批判性阅读的关键动作之一，就是主动追问：有什么重要的信息被省略了？

en.sourceText: A media survey reports that 78% of respondents support building a new viaduct downtown. The report claims residents broadly support the project, so construction should start soon. The survey was funded by the city's transport bureau.【gap:gap1】

textRefs.reason_1: 78% of respondents support building a new viaduct downtown
textRefs.gap1_correct: Respondents volunteered through the transport bureau's website, so the sample skews toward supporters
textRefs.distractor_1: The survey was funded by the city's transport bureau

gap1: Respondents volunteered through the transport bureau's website, so the sample skews toward supporters
The viaduct is expected to take three years to build
The city previously held several public hearings

hints: What is missing from the report? A key piece was torn away
Is '78%' trustworthy? How were respondents chosen?
Who funded the survey and where respondents came from are usually omitted
en.explanation: The report omits the crucial detail: respondents volunteered through the transport bureau's website, so the sample skews toward people who already favored the project. Without it, “78% support” may only echo the voices of those who supported it all along. A key habit of critical reading: always ask — what significant information is omitted?
